summary: G. B. Beaman worked in indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Cincinnati (B.A. ~1889-1893), the University of Jena (1893), and the University of Leipzig (Ph.D. 1894-1895) under Ernst Windisch in 1894.

G. B. Palsule was a scholar of indology and linguistics. He held posts as sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
G. Herberich was an indologist. He completed his Ph.D. in 1893 at the University of Würzburg, where he studied under Julius Jolly.
G. K. Jenkins worked in indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Bloxham School (~1932-1937), he held a post at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera worked in Buddhist studies and indology. He studied at St. John's College, Panadura, University of London, and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He taught at University College, Colombo, and the University of Ceylon.

G. Rita Dudley-Grant, active in Buddhist studies, studied at NHS Grampian (1983-1986) and Robert Gordon University (1994-1997). She held posts at Virgin Islands Behavioral Sciences (attested 2003) and as an advanced practitioner physiotherapist at NHS Grampian (2004).

G. S. Sahay worked in indology and philosophy, serving as Research Officer at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005). He studied at the University of Nebraska Medical Center and held posts at MIT and Oregon State University.
G. Srinivasa Murti was an indologist who served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre, a post attested during 1938-1949 and in 1971.

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University (~1951-1955). He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960-1978) and Columbia University (~1978-2006), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978-2006).
G. V. Aston worked in philosophy and religious studies. Aston earned a Doctor of Philosophy in Philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986-2004), studying under Paul Harrison.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao was a scholar of indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and retired as Senior Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Gabriel Engelsmann was an indologist. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (~1880-1885), where he studied under Georg Bühler (~1881-1885).

Gabriel Jouveau-Dubreuil worked in indology, history, and archaeology. He was Professor of "physique chimie" at Lycée Français de Pondichéry in 1909 and completed a Ph.D. at the University of Paris (~1910-1914).

Gadjin Nagao specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Ryotai Hatani and Susumu Yamaguchi, and later held posts there, including Chair of Buddhist Studies (1935-1971), and at Kyushu University (1956-1958).

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of religious studies and indology. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Galuh Nur Fattah specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. After earning an M.Phil. at Gadjah Mada University (2021-2023), he served as Assistant Professor there (2024-2025) and Lecturer at Sekolah Tinggi Agama Buddha Negeri Raden Wijaya (2025).

Gananath Obeyesekere worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington, later teaching at Ceylon (~1958-1971), Washington (~1966-1972), UC San Diego (~1972-1980), and Princeton University (1980-2000).

Ganesh Prasad worked in indology, history, and archaeology after studying at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He was head of department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held professorships at the University of Calcutta (~1914-1918) and Banaras Hindu University (~1918-1923).

Ganganatha Jha worked in indology and philosophy. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the universities of Calcutta and Allahabad. His main posts included Professor at Muir Central College (1902-1918) and Vice Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923-1932).
